note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Runny nose, nasal congestion, cough, and ear pulling for approximately one day.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 5-year-old male who began feeling ill around supper time last night. Caregiver reports onset of runny nose with nasal congestion. Nasal mucous is currently clear. Patient has a cough that is not barky in character. Patient has been pulling on his ears and rubbing his nose vigorously. Rectal temperature was 100.3°F. Appetite decreased compared to baseline—ate approximately 7 ounces from bottle this morning and refused cereal. Patient is energetic but irritable and fighting sleep. Caregiver notes patient's whole body was sweating when sleeper was removed earlier today despite air conditioning being on.

Exposures: Older sister has been sick. Recent play date with nephew who was later found to have a sinus infection.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Runny nose, nasal congestion, cough (non-barky), ear pulling, nasal rubbing, low-grade fever, decreased appetite, irritability, sleep disturbance, and diaphoresis noted.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Cradle cap.

MEDICATIONS
Saline mist to nose, Tylenol given early this morning, baby Vick's applied to feet last night, humidifier used.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Older sister currently sick with similar symptoms.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally with good air movement.
Ears: Within normal limits.
Overall: Patient doing well during examination.

RESULTS
Clinical presentation consistent with viral upper respiratory infection.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Viral upper respiratory infection. Patient does not require antibiotics at this time. Anticipatory guidance provided regarding progression to bacterial sinusitis. Caregiver to monitor closely for development of barky cough. If barky cough develops, administer half teaspoon of sister's cough medicine for 5 days. Prescribed same cough medicine for patient (half teaspoon dose) to have on hand given weekend timing. For regular cough, may use Zarbee's cough syrup at dose for children under one year of age. Continue saline mist, fluids, and rest. Avoid honey; agave is safe alternative. Counsel caregiver regarding treatment of cradle cap: use dandruff shampoo such as Head & Shoulders, Selsun Blue, or Nizoral AD (regular strength only) twice weekly, continue soft brush with baby oil, and avoid contact with eyes during rinsing. Expect improvement within 6 weeks. Follow-up appointment in one week. Return sooner if condition worsens.
